newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian home ownership cheaper than renting- bank.
newsitem.headline: Canadian home ownership cheaper than renting- bank.

text.p: The cost of financing home ownership in Canada remains cheaper than renting and should become even more affordable in the coming months, the Bank of Montreal said on Monday.
Canada's third-largest bank said its housing attractiveness index rose to 1.16 in May from 1.14 in April.
The rise in the index implies the cost of renting an average three-bedroom apartment was 16 percent higher than monthly interest payments required to own an average starter home.

The bank forecast that home ownership will become even more affordable in the coming months. The affordability index is expected to climb to 1.25 in August, matching the 28-year high it reached in December.
While housing prices have begun to rise, falling mortage rates helped the affordability index rise in May, said Bank of Montreal economist Tim O'Neill.

"Our forecast calls for 338,000 homes to be sold in Canada in 1997, the highest number ever," said O'Neill. "This activity is partly due to the extremely attractive prices of homes compared to available rental accommodation."
